1: ✦In the first week, the baby hasn't actually implanted in your womb yet.✦Pregnancy lasts 40 weeks, but it is counted from the first day of your last period, not from implantation. During the first week, an egg cell starts to develop in your left or right ovary.
2: ✦Before your baby starts growing, you set the stage.✦Last week's rise in estrogen and progestin in your blood prompted your womb to build a rich, blood-filled lining ready for a possible fertilized egg.✦At the same time, eggs are maturing in fluid-filled sacs in your ovaries called follicles.
3: ✦At the start of this week (usually around day 14 of a 28-day cycle) you ovulated.✦One of your eggs left its follicle and travelled to the fallopian tube.✦Over the next 12–24 hours, one of the roughly 250 million sperm released by your partner will swim through the vagina, pass the cervix, enter the womb and try to reach and enter the egg in the fallopian tube.✦If it succeeds, the egg will be fertilized.✦About 400 sperm survive this journey, and only one manages to break through the egg's membrane.
4: ✦Over the next 30 hours, the nuclei of the sperm and the egg will join to combine their genetic material.✦If the sperm carries a Y chromosome, your baby will be a boy; if it carries an X chromosome, you'll have a girl.
5: ✦On its 3–4 day journey from the fallopian tube to the womb, the fertilized egg – the zygote – divides into 16 identical cells.✦Once it reaches the womb, the zygote is called a morula.✦One or two days later it settles into the lining of your womb and continues its amazing development and transformation.
6: ✦At this stage your developing baby is just a tiny ball of cells, scientifically called a blastocyst.✦The blastocyst has an inner cell mass that will form the embryo and an outer cell mass that will form the placenta; there is also a fluid-filled cavity that will become the amniotic sac.✦The outer cell mass becomes the placenta, the organ that brings oxygen and nutrients to your baby and carries waste away.
7: ✦Your last period started 12 to 16 days ago.✦So you're probably ovulating now or will ovulate soon.✦Although pregnancy really lasts about 38 weeks, the exact moment egg and sperm meet can't be known, so doctors calculate the due date as 40 weeks from the start of your last period.✦That's why you're already counted as 2 weeks pregnant when fertilization happens.✦Timing really matters if you want to conceive.✦To improve your chances, have intercourse between 72 hours before and 24 hours after ovulation.✦This lines up the sperm's 72-hour lifespan with the egg's 24-hour lifespan.✦Your partner should keep this window free too.✦To ease the pressure on both of you, it helps to know how long conception usually takes.✦Most couples only announce a pregnancy after several tries.✦If you're trying to conceive and still drink, smoke or take medicines, now is the time to stop.✦Your body should be in the best possible shape for the baby.✦Talk to your doctor about starting folic acid and vitamin supplements to lower the risk of birth defects.
8: ✦In the second week of pregnancy (around day 14 of a 28-day cycle) the released egg is pushed into the fallopian tube.✦Within the next 12 to 24 hours, out of about 250 million sperm making the tough 10-hour journey through the vagina, cervix and uterus to the fallopian tube, around 400 survive and only one enters the egg's membrane.✦The surge in LH peaks within 24 to 36 hours; this process, commonly known as ovulation, ends with the mature egg being fertilized by the right sperm.
9: ✦When the due date is calculated, counting starts before fertilization – from week 2 – even though sperm and egg haven't met yet.✦Women have about a 25% chance of getting pregnant in each menstrual cycle.
10: ✦At 2 weeks, the earliest stage of pregnancy, the sudden rise in estrogen and progesterone can make your breasts extra sensitive.✦But since this is also a symptom of the menstrual cycle, breast changes can't be taken as a definite sign of pregnancy.
11: ✦Most babies are born around this week of the cycle count, but it's usually hard to know exactly when egg and sperm met.✦That's why health providers use 40 weeks from the first day of your last period to estimate the due date.✦These estimates can vary by about 4 weeks depending on the length of your cycle.✦Since some women have shorter or longer cycles, the due date can be pinned down more precisely with an ultrasound.
12: ✦Timing is very important for fertilization.✦Your chances of conceiving are highest in the window around ovulation, roughly two weeks before your next period would start.✦Beyond all this, most couples need more than a few tries before conceiving.✦So it's important to have a full health check-up before deciding to have a baby to make sure you're ready.✦If you take any medication, be sure to tell your doctor and decide whether to continue it during pregnancy.
13: ✦Every baby develops a little differently, even in the womb.✦If you think you need vitamin supplements, talk to your doctor and, if needed, start them from this week.✦Folic acid in particular is very important for the baby's development and for protecting against harm in the womb.✦Also make sure to eat plenty of nutrient-rich fruits and vegetables.
14: ✦Besides building a healthy prenatal diet and exercise routine, this week is the perfect time to quit smoking and alcohol.
15: ✦You're at the start of the first trimester (the first 3 months of pregnancy).✦The first trimester, which lasts until week 13, will be the period of the most change in your life until the moment you hold your baby.✦Mothers-to-be usually realise they're pregnant around this time, after a missed period.
16: ✦Even if you don't look pregnant yet, your body is going through many changes inside and out.✦In the first trimester, when growth is fastest, you'll experience the development of your baby's brain, heart and spine together.
17: ✦Early pregnancy signs at 3 weeks vary from person to person and may include back pain, tiredness and mild cramps.
18: ✦Tender, swollen breasts: many women describe this as much stronger than before a period.✦Exhaustion and tiredness: rising progesterone and your baby's development can make you feel like you've run a marathon.✦Needing to pee often: this starts right after you conceive.✦Heightened sense of smell: smells feeling stronger is a common sign.✦It's caused by the sudden rise in estrogen.✦Food aversions: aversion to certain foods is a more common sign than increased appetite.✦Nausea, vomiting and morning sickness: these usually begin a few weeks later.✦But some mothers-to-be notice them earlier.✦Higher body temperature: if your temperature has been slightly raised for more than 18 days, you're most likely pregnant.✦Light bleeding: you may have light red, pink or brown spotting around the time of your period.✦If you also have severe pain, contact your doctor right away.
19: ✦At this stage, rather than cravings, you may find yourself turning away from foods – things you usually enjoy may suddenly seem off-putting.✦Many smells can also make you gag in early pregnancy.✦This is due to rapidly rising estrogen levels.✦Morning sickness isn't common yet, but in some pregnancies it starts a little earlier.
20: ✦Now is the time to start paying more attention to your health than usual.✦Drinking plenty of water and eating 5 portions of different fruits and vegetables a day is enough for now.✦If you haven't yet, talk to your doctor about starting folic acid supplements.
21: ✦Once you know you're pregnant, pay attention to everything you eat and drink.✦Coffee, tea and alcohol top the list.✦High caffeine intake in pregnancy may raise the risk of miscarriage and low birth weight.✦One cup of coffee a day is generally fine as long as caffeine stays under 200 milligrams.✦Remember tea contains caffeine too, so count it toward your limit.
22: ✦At 4 weeks, your body is changing very actively.✦The changes vary from woman to woman.✦Some experience typical early symptoms like mood swings, nausea and cramps; others have uncomfortable PMS-like symptoms.✦Some women go through this stage without feeling any of these.✦Whether you feel them or not, it may still be too early for a pregnancy test to give a reliable result.
23: ✦This week the fertilized egg and your womb are connected, and your baby – as a blastocyst – starts attaching to the uterine wall.✦In about 30% of pregnancies, implantation bleeding happens as the cell cluster burrows into the uterine wall.✦Implantation bleeding is usually very light and light pink, light red or light brown.✦It happens before your expected period and is not a sign that something is wrong.✦You may feel slight pressure in your belly (nothing to worry about!) and mild breast tenderness and growth (get ready for more growth spurts).
24: ✦The fertilized egg burrows into the womb, and as a result you may have some light bleeding.✦Any pregnancy symptoms at this stage will be very subtle.✦If you're very sensitive, you may notice tiredness, nausea, bloating, tender breasts and changes in hair and skin.
25: ✦Right after a positive pregnancy test, it's a good idea to see a GP or a dentist.✦Dental check-ups during pregnancy are really important.✦Besides caring for your teeth during pregnancy, keep it up during the first 12 months after birth too.
26: ✦This week you may find out whether you're pregnant.✦For a clear result, wait until the end of this week and take a pregnancy test.✦If it's positive, call your doctor and book your first prenatal appointment.✦Many doctors don't schedule the first visit before week eight.✦But if you have a health problem, had a difficult pregnancy before, or have worrying symptoms, call your doctor right away.
27: ✦The next 6 weeks will be very critical for your baby's development.✦The placenta and umbilical cord, still developing, will start taking on their jobs.✦Everything you take in will reach your baby through the placenta and directly affect their health and development.✦So pay close attention to your diet.
28: ✦Welcome to the nausea club! Almost 75% of pregnant women are members.✦So this is something millions of pregnant women go through – no need to worry.
29: ✦This week early pregnancy signs continue while your baby develops rapidly.✦As more signs of pregnancy appear day by day, your sesame-seed-sized baby keeps causing big changes in your body.✦This week you may experience frequent urination, excess saliva, cravings and food aversions.
30: ✦This week the baby is 1.5–2 mm long, about the size of a sesame seed.✦It weighs very little – about 1.5 grams at most.
31: ✦Your baby's development continues excitingly this week.✦Many mothers-to-be wonder if a 5-week baby can be seen on ultrasound.✦The first ultrasound is usually done transvaginally for a better assessment.✦Since the baby is still a rapidly developing cluster of cells, it appears as a tiny white dot.
32: ✦On ultrasound a 5-week baby looks like a tiny tadpole.✦By the end of the week it starts to curve into a C shape, so it's also compared to a shrimp.✦Your doctor will measure your baby's length on the ultrasound.✦From this week the heart starts beating, though you won't hear it on the ultrasound yet.✦The heart, the first organ to start working, beats about 90–100 times a minute this week.✦The spinal cord will start forming between the brain and the tail.
33: ✦Many women have vaginal discharge throughout pregnancy.✦Leukorrhea is a thin, white, mild-smelling or odourless discharge.✦It's caused by hormones and the growing blood flow to the vaginal walls.✦Discharge may increase throughout pregnancy. Its high acidity is thought to help keep harmful bacteria away.
34: ✦You may have light vaginal bleeding or spotting during the first 12 weeks.✦Depending on how heavy, long and frequent it is, bleeding can mean many things.✦It's very important to keep track of it and inform your doctor accurately.✦Note the consistency (watery, thick), colour (light pink, light red, dark red, etc.), duration and frequency, and talk to your doctor.
35: ✦Although it's called morning sickness, nausea isn't limited to mornings.✦It can happen at any time of day.✦It's most common in the first trimester, the first 3 months of pregnancy.✦Signs usually appear between weeks 5 and 8.✦It's expected to ease by weeks 13–14.
36: ✦You may have gained a few kilos by now.✦If you have nausea and can't eat well, you may even have lost weight.✦If this is your first pregnancy, your belly may not have changed much yet, or your waistbands may feel a little tight.✦You may be gaining weight in your legs or breasts.
37: ✦You may feel emotionally up and down – your hormones are at work.✦On top of that, huge changes are coming in your life.✦It's completely natural to feel intense emotions.
38: ✦Light bleeding can happen at this stage.✦It doesn't mean the pregnancy is in trouble.✦But bleeding can also be the first sign of a miscarriage or ectopic pregnancy.✦If you have bleeding, it's still advisable to tell your doctor.
39: ✦About 1 in 31 births is twins.✦Without fertility treatment, the chance drops to about 1 in 89.✦The chance of triplets (or more) is about 1 in 565.✦Identical twins usually happen by chance, about 1 in 250.✦20–25% of women who have fertility treatment conceive twins (or more).✦Your chance of twins can also depend on other factors.✦If you've had twins before, your chance of having twins again doubles.✦If there are twins in your or your partner's family, your chance is higher.✦The older you are, the higher the chance of naturally conceiving twins (or more).✦The more pregnancies you've had, the higher your chance.✦Twins are more common in tall, slim women and less common in shorter women.
40: ✦It's very important to avoid foods and drinks that could harm you or your baby during pregnancy.✦But there's a lot of misinformation about which foods are good or bad.✦You don't want to skip healthy foods or stress about your diet because of it.✦So learn now which foods and drinks to avoid.✦At 6 weeks, keeping a list of these on your fridge can help.
41: ✦From the first weeks of pregnancy, the mother's metabolism speeds up a lot to meet the baby's needs.✦The amount of blood pumped from the heart to the organs and skin increases by about 40%.✦Your blood volume will increase by nearly 50%.
42: ✦At 6 weeks, changes in the mother become noticeable.✦Breast tenderness, growth and darkening of the nipples are signs of 6 weeks of pregnancy.✦Fat starts building up around the waist.
43: ✦All roads lead to the bathroom.✦Surging hormones and increased blood volume make your body produce more fluid, so you'll find yourself heading to the toilet more often than ever.✦But keeping your body well hydrated is important, so keep drinking extra water throughout pregnancy.
44: ✦Healthy habits.✦During pregnancy, order your meat well done and stay away from cat litter.✦Toxoplasmosis, an infection spread by raw meat and cat faeces, can be harmful to your baby (though not to you).✦You may already have had it without knowing – in that case you're immune.
45: ✦Keep drinking plenty of water, even if it means more trips to the toilet.✦Make sure the meat you eat is well cooked.✦If there's a flu outbreak, get vaccinated (ask your doctor).
